title: Count rows in each group
summary: GROUP BY puts matching values together. An aggregate such as count gives one answer for each group.
introduction: GROUP BY puts matching values together. An aggregate such as count gives one answer for each group. Your task: Add another science row and predict the counts.

blocks.text: GROUP BY puts matching values together. An aggregate such as count gives one answer for each group.
Use PostgreSQL in a new practice database through psql or a database editor. These are PostgreSQL examples, not SQLite. They do not run in this site's SQL playground. Use only sample data.

blocks.code:
WITH books(kind) AS (VALUES ('story'),('science'),('story'))
SELECT kind,count(*) AS book_count FROM books GROUP BY kind ORDER BY kind;
blocks.title: Count rows in each group

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `ORDER BY` chooses a result order. Include a tie-break field when equal values need a stable order.
`GROUP BY` makes one summary group for each distinct combination of the named grouping values.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: Science has 1 book and story has 2.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Every selected non-aggregate value needs a suitable grouping rule. Do not choose an unrelated title from each group.
